Dear Jill,

I will let Meena comment on the specific error message. However, from the initial problem description it appears that you have multiple repetitions of a same feature in what MSstats thinks is a single run. If in reality the features were quantified in multiple runs, you need to check whether the 'Run' column in the Skyline report correctly reflects your experiment.

Please let us know if this doesn't help

Sincerely

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: MSstat as external tool in skyline_duplicate rows
parts:
Dear Jill,

MSstats recognizes MS runs from raw file names. If you have multiple runs in one .wiff file, MSstats will have multiple measurements in a single run. That's why the first says there are multiple rows. I think that separate wiff files for each run are the best and easiest solution. If you are familiar with changing Skyline report format, and know which measurements for features are from which MS runs, you can use MSstats directly from updated MSstats report.

I hope it is helpful for you.

--Meena
